match.reason: The bank point teaches marketing approaches (relationship and societal marketing) rather than the macro-environment idea that shifting societal values and trends change what customers want, so it is a different idea.

draft.title: Societal attitudes
card: Societal attitudes are the values, beliefs and trends shared by many people in a community. They are part of the social factors in the macro environment, so a business cannot control them.

When attitudes shift, what customers want shifts too. More care for the environment can lead people to look for products with less packaging. A wish to eat healthily can lead people to choose fresh food.
A business that notices a shift early can change its products, ingredients or marketing to match. A business that ignores it may lose customers to rivals who adapt.
Attitudes differ between age groups, places and cultures, and they change over time. Planners watch for changes by reading research, surveys and trends before they set up.
draft.remember: Customers' values change over time, and a business plans around those changes.

a.q: More people in Geelong now say they want to cut down on waste. Which change by a new café is the best match to this shift?
opts: Serving takeaway drinks in reusable cups
Cutting the price of its takeaway coffee
Opening an hour earlier on weekdays
Adding free wifi for customers to use
a.why: The shift is a change in values about waste, so the café matches it by offering reusable cups. A lower coffee price or longer hours may attract customers, but they do not respond to the new attitude.
a.clue: Which change speaks to the value people now hold?

b.q: Priya plans a lunch bar in Ballarat. Surveys show more locals want healthy food. She keeps her fried menu and does not change it. What is the most likely risk?
opts: Customers may choose rivals that offer healthier food
The council may refuse to register her business
Interest rates may rise and make her loan costlier
Suppliers may stop selling her cooking oil
b.why: The shift in attitudes changes what customers want, so a menu that ignores it may lose sales to rivals that adapt. Registration and loan costs belong to other factors, and nothing in the case points to them.
b.clue: Ask what the survey says about what customers want.

a.best: Serving takeaway drinks in reusable cups

b.best: Customers may choose rivals that offer healthier food
